title: 01 / Contour type
idea: The same skeleton becomes a landscape of merging outlines.
limitation: At large offsets, nearby letters merge. This is a field effect, not an independent outline per glyph.

title: 02 / Living strokes
idea: Thicker junctions and wandering strands make the word feel grown.
limitation: Individual pen paths are the unit. Dense intersections and pen-lift count need a physical specimen.

title: 03 / Patterned face
idea: A closed letter silhouette gives texture a precise place to live.
limitation: Use Outline and Depth 0 on Lettering. Pattern Fill preserves nested holes.

title: 04 / Modular squares
idea: Letter ink becomes a field of small drawn squares.
limitation: Image interprets the drawing as a raster internally, then emits pen paths. The square size limits fine details.

title: 05 / Serpentine type
idea: Each stroke is replaced by a dense, rounded zigzag.
limitation: Amplitude can close small counters. Fine waves cost more plot length than the original skeleton.

title: 06 / Along a path
idea: An existing drawing becomes a baseline for repeated words.
limitation: Letters sit on local tangents. They are not warped continuously through the bend.

title: 07 / Modular marks
idea: The existing stitch engine already separates core, edge and halo.
limitation: This uses the built-in bitmap alphabet. Different mark types can share the same letter layout.

title: 08 / Hairline lettering
idea: A complete text engine for letters made of parallel ribbons.
limitation: Current alphabet is lowercase a–z; capitals fold to lowercase and digits / punctuation are skipped.

title: 09 / Flow around a word
idea: A word becomes an obstacle and organises its surrounding space.
limitation: Closed obstacles use polygon union. This is an exterior-flow study; enclosed letter counters are blocked.

title: 10 / Words inside a word
idea: A large letterform holds a field of smaller text.
limitation: Region tests glyph centres, not complete stroke containment. Small letters can cross the large outline at the edges.

title: 11 / Falling characters
idea: A single letter can already be used as a stamp in a collapsing grid.
limitation: This repeats the input as one motif. Dissolving an arbitrary sentence letter by letter needs a different, glyph-aware mode.

title: 12 / Text made of text
idea: Small plotted characters become the tone of a larger word.
limitation: Hatching supplies line density. A bare thin outline gives a different, much lighter ASCII interpretation.
